flow.costPlain: What Block pays to run each transaction and product: card-network fees for sellers, the cost of Cash App's money features, and the bitcoin Block buys to resell — $1,863M of the total is bitcoin cost alone.

opex.name: Product development
opex.note: Engineers and designers building Square, Cash App and Block's bitcoin products.

opex.name: Sales and marketing
opex.note: Winning sellers for Square and new users for Cash App, including Cash App peer-to-peer processing costs.

opex.name: General and administrative
opex.note: Running the company — finance, legal, people and offices. Down from $728M a year ago, when it carried heavy litigation and regulatory accruals.

opex.name: Transaction & loan losses
opex.note: Money Block expects not to collect on Cash App Borrow, Afterpay and seller loans — the cost of being a lender. More than double the $245M a year ago as lending volumes surged.

opex.name: Amortization
opex.note: Spreading the cost of companies Block has bought.

follow100Note: For every $100 of revenue, Block's products earned $45.94 of gross profit — then running costs left $7.76 of operating income, and a $234M bitcoin paper loss plus tax left $1.85 of net income per $100. Rows may not add exactly due to rounding.
footerNote: Net income attributable to common stockholders was $116M.

oneTimers: A $234M non-cash loss from revaluing Block's bitcoin holdings (a $252M gain a year ago) sits below operating income — the main reason GAAP net income of $116M trails adjusted net income of $402M.
Operating expenses include $54M of contingencies, restructuring and other charges.

Adjusted figures strip out share-based compensation, amortization, contingencies and restructuring charges: adjusted operating income was $588M versus $485M GAAP, and adjusted EPS was $0.65 versus $0.19 GAAP.
otherDetail: Interest expense, net of $54M and a $234M paper loss from revaluing Block's bitcoin holdings, partly offset by $5M of other income — a net $283M cost below operating income.
pngFooterNote: Bitcoin paper loss shrank the quarter — see one-time items.

segments.name: Commerce enablement
segments.note: Square's business: payment processing and tools for sellers, plus Cash App's commerce features. Square's gross payment volume grew 10% — international volume up 24% — and gross profit from this category rose 11% to $1,623M.

segments.name: Financial solutions
segments.note: Cash App's money products — Borrow loans, Afterpay buy-now-pay-later, the Cash App Card and banking features. Gross profit jumped 51% to $1,132M as consumer lending origination volume grew 69%. Costs were just $91M against $1,222M of revenue.

segments.name: Bitcoin ecosystem
segments.note: Bitcoin bought and sold through Cash App, plus Block's bitcoin hardware and mining efforts. Revenue fell as bitcoin trading cooled; $1,863M of costs against $1,980M of revenue left just $118M of gross profit, up 10%.

sources.label: Form 10-Q for the quarter ended Sep 30, 2025 (SEC EDGAR) — nine-month figures used to derive Q4 line items

takeaways.text: Gross profit rose 24% to $2,872M — Cash App contributed $1,831M (+33%) and Square $993M (+7%) — beating Block's guidance. Block raised its full-year 2026 gross profit guidance to $12.20B, up 18%.
takeaways.title: Gross profit growth accelerated

takeaways.text: Adjusted operating income grew 46% to $588M — a 20% margin on gross profit — putting Block's Rule of 40 at 44% (24% growth plus 20% margin). The same day, Block announced plans to cut headcount nearly in half, from over 10,000 to just under 6,000, betting on AI-led productivity.
takeaways.title: Adjusted profit hit a new gear

takeaways.text: A $234M non-cash loss from revaluing Block's bitcoin holdings, versus a $252M gain a year ago, pulled GAAP net income to $116M (EPS $0.19) against $0.65 adjusted. The year-ago $1,946M net income also included a $1.9B one-time tax benefit, so the drop overstates any slowdown.
takeaways.title: Bitcoin's paper loss shrank the bottom line

verdict: Block's gross profit jumped 24% to $2.9B as Cash App surged 33%, but a $234M paper loss on its bitcoin holdings held net income to just $116M.
